Every push to `main` appends one line to `bench-history.jsonl` on the `bench-history` branch, and keeps the
JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

JSON of every round as a workflow artifact. Each line is a controlled measurement: the job measures the pushed
commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:

commit and its first parent on the same runner, interleaved, the way a pull request compares base and head. A line
holds, per case, the parent median, the commit median and the change in percent, plus the runner identity (OS,
architecture, CPU model) and the Bun version. Absolute medians are only comparable within one line, because runners
differ by up to 2.5x; the trend to read is the change per commit. Lines written before this format hold one
uncontrolled median per case; they are still read, and the table shows `n/a` for their change. History jobs run one
at a time; a merge that lands while two others wait can be skipped, which leaves a gap and nothing else. A table of
the trend:
